subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - p95/p99 latency & throughput AB test next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@globex.com>, Tom Herrera <tom.herrera@globex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - p95/p99 latency & throughput AB test next steps

Hi Ava / Tom —

Thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum from the discovery: 

Summary of where we landed:
- Primary goal: validate production latency (p95/p99) and sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for your chat use case (~1.2k tokens/session, 30 concurrent sessions)
- Baseline: your current hyperscaler endpoint (Tom)
- What Globex wants to see: p95/p99, median, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and stability under 95th percentile load spikes

Proposed short A/B test plan (what we recommend running next):
1) Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler baseline on same sequence-length profile (1.2k median)
2) Run 3 x 15-minute steady-state runs at target concurrency (30 sessions) to collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec
3) Run 2 x 10-minute spike tests (100 concurrent sessions) to observe fallback/queueing behavior
4) Capture KV/cache hit rates, batching size distribution, and memory footprint per model variant

Action items / owners:
- Globex: share any existing request/response sample traces and preferred tokenization profile (Tom / Ava) — due Wed 3/3
- Redwood (Rafael): schedule Dedicated run and provide run config + expected timeframe — due Fri 3/5
- Redwood (Marissa): provide mutual action plan + test template and a brief deck summarizing differentiators — sent with this thread

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (template with checkpoints)

Proposed time to sync after runs: 1 hour review on Mon 3/8 (I can block 10-11 PT if that works).

Thanks — looking forward to validating with numbers.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (555) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - p95/p99 latency & throughput AB test next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with our needs. A few clarifying items from our side before we kick off: 

1) Tokenization: we use GPT-style tokenization, average session ~1.2k tokens but tail up to 2.5k in ~5% of sessions. Please include a separate run for 2.5k sequences.
2) Cost calc: can you confirm how you account for cache hits versus full-generation tokens for cost per 1M tokens?
3) Hyperscaler baseline: we can share an anonymized trace and preliminary baseline numbers. See attached initial run export (globex_abtest_results_v1.csv) — this is a 10-minute snapshot at 30 concurrency.

Two small asks:
- Please add an explicit p99 cold-start check (single warmup request after a 30s idle)
- Can you confirm Redwood's quantization profile for the model variant you'll test?

We'll get the trace + a little more context (tokenization/profile) by EOD Wed 3/3.

Appreciate it — Ava

--
Ava Collins
Sr. Manager, ML Platforms | Globex Corporation
ava.collins@globex.com | (212) 555-0146

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - p95/p99 latency & throughput AB test next steps

Ava —

Perfect, thanks for sending the CSV. Quick answers inline and updated plan: 

- Tokenization: noted on 2.5k tail — we'll add one dedicated run at 2.5k sequence length.
- Cost calc: our evaluation will report both "billed tokens" and "effective tokens" (post-cache delta). We'll include cost per 1M billed tokens and an adjusted cost accounting for observed prefix cache hits during the run.
- Cold-start p99: we will include a cold-start p99 check as requested.
- Quantization: we'll run the recommended 8-bit quantized variant for the public model you pointed to; final config will be in the run config Rafael shares.

Next steps (updated):
- Rafael to schedule Dedicated cluster run and post run-config YAML in this thread (ETA: Fri 3/5)
- We'll run: 3 x 15-min steady at 30 concurrency (1.2k), 1 x 15-min steady at 2.5k, 2 x 10-min spikes at 100 concurrency, plus cold-start checks
- Deliverables: CSV raw output, summary PDF (redwood_vs_cloud_latency_report.pdf), and cost delta calculation

I'll schedule the Mon 3/8 review tentatively and send a calendar invite once Rafael confirms run times.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - run config and measurement checklist (internal)

Rafael / Lukas —

Looping you both in with the test ask from Globex. Please use the following minimal run configuration and measurement checklist. Rafael, can you confirm estimated slot usage and ETA for running these on Dedicated?

Run config (minimal):
- Model: opt-70b-8q (prod-serving variant, 8-bit quantized)
- Sequence lengths: 1.2k (primary), 2.5k (tail)
- Concurrency: steady 30, spikes at 100
- Runs: steady (3x 15m at 30), tail steady (1x 15m at 2.5k), spikes (2x 10m at 100), cold-start checks (5 single requests after 30s idle)
- Measurement cadence: 1s sampling for tokens/sec; 100ms histogram buckets for latency to compute p50/p95/p99
- Logging: per-request latency, batch size, KV-cache hit flag, memory usage, and CPU/GPU utilization

Success metrics to capture: p95 and p99 (latency), sustained tokens/sec (avg and 95th), tail error rates, retry rates, and cost per 1M billed tokens

Artifacts to produce: raw CSV, summarized PDF (including cost calc), and a brief run-note describing any infra-related anomalies

Notes:
- Keep the environment identical across Redwood runs (same model binary, same runtime flags) to ensure apples-to-apples vs hyperscaler baseline
- Use the same tokenization profile that Ava provided

Can you ack and share run slot ETA? If we can run Thursday 3/4 (overnight) we can get results back Friday and still meet the proposed Mon review.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>

Marissa —

Acked. Quick update on scheduling and a short preview of initial numbers from a smoke run we started to sanity-check configs: 

Scheduling:
- I reserved 4 Dedicated slots for Thu 3/4 02:00-06:00 PT (overnight run). That should cover the steady runs + spikes.
- ETA for full deliverables (CSV + PDF): Fri 3/5 EOD PST

Smoke-run preview (10-minute sanity run, 30 concurrency, 1.2k seq):
- median latency: 120 ms
- p95 latency: 310 ms
- p99 latency: 520 ms
- sustained tokens/sec (aggregate): ~18.4k tokens/sec (server-side aggregate across slots)
- observed average batch size: 5.2
- KV-cache hit rate (simulated prefix reuse): ~22%

Notes: numbers look reasonable and roughly in line with our internal expectations versus the hyperscaler sample trace Ava shared. We'll run the full battery Thursday night and attach the redwood_vs_cloud_latency_report.pdf with full comparisons.

I'll post the full run-config YAML and the raw CSVs once the runs complete.
